title: Erdős Problem #617 — Missing Colors in Complete-Graph Colorings
statement: Let $r\geq3$. If the edges of the complete graph $K_{r^2+1}$ are colored with $r$ colors, must there exist $r+1$ vertices such that one color is absent from all edges among those vertices? Equivalently, for every finite vertex set $V$ with $|V|=r^2+1$ and every coloring of the unordered pairs of vertices by the colors in $\{0,\ldots,r-1\}$, there exist a subset $S\subseteq V$ with $|S|=r+1$ and a color $k$ such that no edge between two distinct vertices of $S$ has color $k$.
source_name: The Formal Conjectures Authors, Formal Conjectures (2025); independently edited from the pinned source file.
